name: TutorLaunch Orchestrator: Evidence-to-Funded-Program Builder
description: An end-to-end meta-workflow that stands up a fundable, evidence-based K-12 or adult tutoring program by chaining three skills: it mines the tutoring research literature into a working intervention/data platform (PaperToPipeline), vets and formalizes tutor staffing credentials (ResumeTruthGuard), then assembles a grant-ready funding proposal (GrantForge Orchestrator) — turning a raw program idea into a defensible, staffed, and funded launch package.

spec.name: TutorLaunch Orchestrator: Evidence-to-Funded-Program Builder
spec.description: An end-to-end meta-workflow that stands up a fundable, evidence-based K-12 or adult tutoring program by chaining three skills: it mines the tutoring research literature into a working intervention/data platform (PaperToPipeline), vets and formalizes tutor staffing credentials (ResumeTruthGuard), then assembles a grant-ready funding proposal (GrantForge Orchestrator) — turning a raw program idea into a defensible, staffed, and funded launch package.
spec.purpose: Transform a high-level tutoring program concept (audience, subject, goals, budget ceiling) into a launch-ready package that is evidence-grounded, staffed with verified tutors, and backed by a submission-ready grant proposal — so program directors can go from idea to funded pilot without stitching the pieces together manually.
instructions: Parse the {{input}} to extract the program's target population (K-12 grade band or adult learner segment), subject area, learning outcomes, measurement horizon, staffing pool (tutor resumes/CVs), and funding target with any named grant/funder.

STEP 1 — Evidence & data foundation: Invoke PaperToPipeline (@kmd_ai/papertopipeline-literature-driven-data-platform-bootstrapper) on the target population + subject to surface the strongest tutoring-efficacy literature and bootstrap a measurement data platform. Capture the recommended intervention design (dosage, group size, cadence), the outcome metrics/instruments to track, and the pipeline schema for logging sessions and progress.

STEP 2 — Staffing verification: For each tutor resume in the pool, invoke ResumeTruthGuard (@kmd_ai/resumetruthguard) to fact-check credentials, flag unverifiable or exaggerated claims, and produce a cleaned, defensible qualifications summary. Aggregate into a staffing table that maps verified tutor competencies to the subject/grade requirements from Step 1.

STEP 3 — Fit check & gap analysis: Cross-reference the verified staffing table (Step 2) against the evidence-based intervention design (Step 1). Identify staffing gaps (e.g., missing certifications, insufficient subject depth) and note them as risks or hiring needs to carry into the proposal.

STEP 4 — Funding assembly: Invoke GrantForge Orchestrator (@kmd_ai/grantforge-orchestrator), feeding it the evidence base and data-tracking plan (Step 1), the verified staffing roster and gap analysis (Steps 2-3), and the funding target. Generate the narrative, logic model, evaluation plan, and budget justification aligned to the funder's priorities.

STEP 5 — Coherence pass: Ensure the metrics named in the grant's evaluation plan exactly match the pipeline schema from Step 1, and that every staff claim in the proposal traces back to a ResumeTruthGuard-verified line — never surface an unverified credential in a funding document.

STEP 6 — Deliver a single Launch Package: (a) evidence summary + intervention design, (b) data platform/measurement plan, (c) verified staffing roster with flagged gaps, (d) submission-ready grant proposal, and (e) a prioritized next-actions checklist (hires needed, data setup, submission deadline).

examples.title: Middle-school math intervention pilot
examples.input: We want to launch an after-school 6th-8th grade math tutoring pilot for a Title I district. Goal: raise state math proficiency by one performance level in one school year. Staffing pool: 4 tutor resumes attached (2 former teachers, 2 college math majors). Target funder: state DOE 21st Century Community Learning Centers grant, ceiling $180k.
examples.output:
LAUNCH PACKAGE

A) EVIDENCE & INTERVENTION DESIGN (via PaperToPipeline): High-dosage tutoring literature supports 3x/week, ~30-min sessions, tutor-to-student ratio ≤1:3 for measurable middle-grade math gains. Recommended instruments: district benchmark assessments + curriculum-aligned unit checks. Intervention: 30-week cycle, twice-weekly small groups.

B) DATA PLATFORM: Session-log schema (student_id, date, dosage_min, group_size, skill_tag, mastery_score) + pre/mid/post benchmark table; dashboard tracking proficiency-level movement toward the one-level-gain goal.

C) VERIFIED STAFFING ROSTER (via ResumeTruthGuard): Tutor A — teaching cert verified, 6 yrs middle math (confirmed). Tutor B — 'lead math coach' title UNVERIFIED, downgraded to 'math tutor, 2 yrs'. Tutors C & D — degrees-in-progress verified. GAP: only 1 of 4 has classroom management credential; recommend 1 additional certified lead or PD.

D) GRANT PROPOSAL (via GrantForge): 21st CCLC-aligned narrative, logic model linking dosage→mastery→proficiency gain, evaluation plan using the exact Step B metrics, $178k budget (staffing, curriculum, assessment tools, eval). Every staff claim traces to verified lines only.

E) NEXT ACTIONS: 1) Hire/PD one certified lead (gap) — before term start. 2) Stand up session-log pipeline — 3 wks. 3) Baseline benchmark before week 1. 4) Submit grant by DOE deadline.

examples.title: Adult ESL literacy program
examples.input: Nonprofit wants a workplace ESL literacy tutoring program for adult immigrant workers, goal: measurable gains in workplace communication over 6 months. 3 tutor CVs attached. Seeking $75k from a regional community foundation.
examples.output:
LAUNCH PACKAGE

A) EVIDENCE & INTERVENTION (PaperToPipeline): Adult ESL research favors contextualized, task-based instruction, 2x/week 60-min, small cohorts; use BEST Plus / workplace-task rubrics as outcome instruments over the 6-month horizon.

B) DATA PLATFORM: Schema logging learner_id, session_date, task_type, CASAS/BEST-level, self-efficacy survey; growth dashboard vs. baseline.

C) VERIFIED ROSTER (ResumeTruthGuard): Tutor 1 — TESOL cert verified. Tutor 2 — 'native-level fluency in 5 languages' flagged as unverifiable, reworded to documented languages. Tutor 3 — adult-ed experience verified. GAP: no assessment-administration training; add short certification.

D) GRANT PROPOSAL (GrantForge): Community-foundation narrative, logic model, evaluation plan matched to Step B instruments, $74k budget. Only verified credentials cited.

E) NEXT ACTIONS: 1) Certify a tutor to administer assessments. 2) Recruit employer partner cohort. 3) Configure data pipeline + baseline. 4) Submit to foundation cycle.

tests.name: Chains all three skills in correct order
tests.input: Launch a 3rd-5th grade reading tutoring program, one attached tutor resume, seeking $50k from a local education foundation.
tests.expected: Output is a single Launch Package that (1) first derives an evidence-based reading intervention + data schema via PaperToPipeline, (2) verifies the tutor resume via ResumeTruthGuard and flags unverifiable claims, (3) produces a GrantForge proposal whose evaluation metrics match the data schema and whose staff claims trace only to verified credentials, and (4) ends with a prioritized next-actions checklist including gap-driven hiring and submission deadline.

tests.name: Never surfaces unverified credentials in the grant
tests.input: Program with one tutor whose resume claims a PhD that cannot be verified; seeking grant funding.
tests.expected: The verified staffing roster marks the PhD claim as unverified/removed, the gap analysis notes it, and the grant proposal section cites only verified qualifications — the unverified PhD does NOT appear as an asserted credential anywhere in the funding narrative.
